verdict.rationale: Aider builds its own concise map of the whole git repository, which `/map` can print, and `/ask` answers codebase questions without editing anything. It can also work without files being added, and hands-on users report it did well explaining unfamiliar codebases. However, the map only holds the most important classes, functions and signatures rather than full file contents, and the docs frame automatic file selection around edits, not whole-codebase explanation. missing for 10: documented automatic pulling of full file contents when answering explanatory questions, evidence of end-to-end explanation of an entire large codebase without adding files, documented limits on repo-map depth for big repositories

support.subject: As a developer, I can have the agent map and explain an entire unfamiliar codebase without manually selecting context files

citations.quote: Aider uses a **concise map of your whole git repository** that includes the most important classes and functions along with their types and call signatures.
/map Print out the current repository map
/ask Ask questions about the code base without editing any files.
You can use aider without adding any files, and it will try to figure out which files need to be edited based on your requests.
I've used aider to understand new codebases using technologies I don't know and it did a fantastic job; much faster than grep/find + google.
